notes: Inbound from product hunt signup → demo request via site form (2/7)
Key contact: Priya Nair (Head of Product). Also engaged CTO: Ben Romero.
Primary ask: replace rule-based summarizer with LLM-driven ticket summarization + structured JSON output to feed their triage pipeline.
They already run a lightweight agent that calls external ticketing APIs (Zendesk) — want LLM to emit explicit tool-call args (ticket_id, tags, priority) rather than free text.
Quote from Priya: 'We need deterministic output so our orchestration can trust the payload — not freeform text that needs regex hacks.'
Self-serve intent: signed up, used free credits, ran static prompts with open models but saw hallucinations/invalid JSON frequently.
Cost sensitivity: high — team wants per-ticket cost < $0.02 at scale; willing to accept smaller model + batching if quality acceptable.
Latency/throughput: p50 < 300ms desired for single-turn summarization; expected steady traffic ~30-60 rps during business hours, spikes to 200rps during incidents.
Model preference: prefer deterministic small/med open models (7B-13B) with a fallback to ultra-low-cost micro-model for non-critical summarization.
Security: must integrate SSO for product admin, need audit logs for generated outputs and user prompts; data retention policy — 30d by default, option to purge.
Their infra: multi-tenant SaaS on GCP (us-central); prefer Redwood hosted API in public cloud region US.
Supporting artifacts: shared sample ticket corpus (anonymized) + current regex-based mapping rules (drive link).
Short-term win: prove >90% valid structured outputs for 5k-ticket sample with minimal post-processing.
Long-term: look at Dedicated once throughput grows and SLA required (12–18 months).
